tips.title: Prepare an emergency kit
tips.body: Water, non-perishable food, flashlight, radio, first-aid kit, documents and a whistle.

tips.title: Secure your home
tips.body: Anchor shelves and heavy objects; identify safe spots under sturdy furniture.

tips.title: Agree on a meeting point
tips.body: Choose a family meeting place and an out-of-town contact.

tips.title: Drop, cover and hold on
tips.body: Protect your head and neck under sturdy furniture until the shaking stops.

tips.title: Stay away from windows
tips.body: Avoid glass, façades and falling objects. Don’t use elevators.

tips.title: If you’re outdoors or driving
tips.body: Move to an open area away from cables and buildings; if driving, stop safely.

steps.caption: Cover your head until it stops

tips.title: Check for injuries and expect aftershocks
tips.body: Treat injuries, stay calm and be ready for aftershocks.

tips.title: Shut off the gas if you smell a leak
tips.body: Turn off the gas, don’t use flames or switches, and ventilate the area.

tips.title: Communicate by text message
tips.body: Use text messages to avoid overloading networks and check on your neighbors.

tips.title: Mental-health line: 192, option 4
tips.body: Free, 24-hour national psychological support. In Bogotá you can also call Line 106. If life is at risk, call 123.

tips.title: Your reactions are normal
tips.body: Fear, insomnia, sadness or anger after a quake are common responses. Talk about how you feel and don’t face it alone.

tips.title: Techniques to calm down
tips.body: Breathe slowly (inhale 4s, exhale 6s), keep sleep and meal routines, and limit exposure to disaster news and images.

steps.caption: Feel your feet on the ground

tips.title: Support children
tips.body: Listen to them, answer calmly and honestly, keep routines and remind them they are safe. Seek professional help if distress persists.

tips.title: Support content (community)
tips.body: Informational Instagram account: @saludmental_paracolombia. It’s a community resource, not an official emergency line; in a crisis use Line 192 (option 4) or 123.

tips.title: If you evacuate, take your pet
tips.body: Never leave it behind. Use a carrier or leash, bring water, some food and an ID tag with your phone number. Keep it close, tagged or microchipped.

tips.title: Shelters receiving aid
tips.body: Several affected foundations accept food, medicine and supplies (e.g. in Pereira, Armenia, Manizales and Villa María). Verify the channels before donating; many are shared via Protección Animal Javeriana.

tips.title: Veterinary care
tips.body: Vets and clinics are treating affected pets in quake areas (e.g. Royi Pets in Cali takes in disoriented animals). Confirm availability before traveling there.

tips.title: Lost-pet finder
tips.body: The community platform “Buscador de Personas y Mascotas — terremoto Colombia” lets you report and search for missing pets. It’s a community resource; verify details before acting.
